item.title: Mariners manager Dan Wilson out after disappointing 2026 campaign
item.description: The Seattle Mariners announced shortly after Sunday's season finale that manager Dan Wilson will not return in 2027.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Seattle Mariners announced shortly after Sunday's season finale that manager Dan Wilson will not return in 2027. Seattle was a disappointing 76-86 this season, finished third in the American League West and missed the playoffs one year after advancing to Game 7 of the 2025 ALCS before falling to the Toronto Blue Jays. Wilson, 57, went 187-171 in two-plus seasons with the Mariners. He reportedly informed the players before Sunday's 7-3 win over the Los Angeles Angels that he wouldn't return. "Collectively we failed to meet our own expectations this season," Seattle president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto said in a news release. "Dan and I both care deeply about this organization, these players, and the future of the Mariners. After much discussion it was concluded that a new direction is best for 2027 and beyond. "I want to thank Dan for his efforts over the past two years and specifically recognize his role in our club advancing to Game 7 of the ALCS in 2025." Energized by Cal Raleigh's 60-homer season, the Mariners went 90-72 and won the AL West last season before beating the Detroit Tigers in five games in the AL Division Series. Seattle had a 3-2 lead in the ALCS before the Blue Jays won the final two games. "I've appreciated the opportunity to lead this team the past two years," Wilson said in the news release. "While this season has not gone the way any of us expected, I'm proud that the players in the clubhouse showed up each day to try and compete and battle in each game they played. I'm confident that the 2026 season doesn't accurately reflect the talent, passion and desire of our players and know that bright things are ahead for this group." Wilson replaced Scott Servais as manager in August 2024 despite not having previous managerial experience. Wilson was a popular player for Seattle (1994-2005) and was an All-Star catcher in 1996 when he established career highs of 18 homers and 83 RBIs. He played in 1,251 games for the team and was a member of four Mariners postseason teams. In August, Wilson was named to the 50 Greatest Mariners team. He also played two seasons for the Cincinnati Reds (1992-93). Wilson is expected to be offered a job to remain with the Mariners. "I want to add my thanks to Dan for the work he's done as manager," Seattle managing partner John Stanton said in the news release. "I have also spoken with Dan and made it clear that we would like to keep him in our organization. I look forward to continued conversations as we work to identify a role in which we can continue to benefit from his experience and commitment to the Mariners and our community." --Field Level Media

item.title: NIO inks battery-swapping deal with Geely, values energy unit at $2.4 billion
item.description: Chinese electric vehicle maker NIO said on Monday it had signed a broad deal with Zhejiang Geely Holding Group on their battery-swapping and charging businesses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese electric vehicle maker NIO (9866.HK) said on Monday it had signed a broad deal with Zhejiang Geely Holding Group on their battery-swapping and charging businesses. Under the deal, Geely Holding Group will acquire a 30% stake in NIO Power, NIO's battery-swapping and charging unit. For the purchase, Geely will contribute its 100% equity in its battery-swapping subsidiary Yiyi Power, plus 640 million yuan ($95 million) in cash. The transaction values NIO Power at a post-money valuation of about 16 billion yuan ($2.38 billion). NIO will acquire a 10% equity stake in Geely's smart charging subsidiary, Haohan Energy. The two companies will co-develop unified swapping standards and vehicle models. NIO Power aims to have 10,000 battery swap stations in operation by 2030, with annual electricity demand expected to exceed 10 billion kWh. Geely plans to expand its network to over 22,000 charging stations with more than 100,000 connectors by the end of 2027. ($1 = 6.7128 Chinese yuan renminbi)

item.title: Raiders rally past Saints for surprise 3-0 start
item.description: Kirk Cousins passed for 248 yards and three touchdowns and the visiting Las Vegas Raiders stayed unbeaten by charging past the New Orleans Saints 35-27 on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kirk Cousins passed for 248 yards and three touchdowns and the visiting Las Vegas Raiders stayed unbeaten by charging past the New Orleans Saints 35-27 on Sunday. Brock Bowers had a standout season debut, returning from a knee injury to catch 10 passes for 116 yards and one touchdown for the surprising Raiders (3-0), who trailed by 11 at one point in the second half. Tyler Shough passed for 255 yards and four touchdowns, but had two costly second-half turnovers for the Saints (1-2). Chris Olave hauled in nine passes for 107 yards, and Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant caught two touchdowns apiece. On their first possession of the second half, the Saints drove 87 yards in 12 plays capped by Shough's 1-yard touchdown pass to Johnson for a 20-16 lead. On the ensuing kickoff, Dylan Laube fumbled and Jordan Howden recovered for New Orleans at the Las Vegas 32. Two plays later, Shough threw a 16-yard touchdown pass to Fant for a 27-16 lead. Mike Washington Jr. ran 36 yards for a touchdown and Cousins' two-point conversion pass went incomplete, leaving the Raiders behind 27-22 at the end of the third quarter. New Orleans was in position to score again until Shough fumbled while being sacked and Maxx Crosby recovered for the Raiders at their 45. That led to Cousins' 4-yard touchdown pass to Cody White, giving Las Vegas a 28-27 lead after Cousins was sacked on a two-point conversion play. Three plays later, Shough was intercepted by Hezekiah Masses and the Raiders took over at the Saints' 4. Cousins' 4-yard touchdown pass to Bowers pushed the lead to 35-27. The Raiders drove to the Saints' 17 on their first possession before Matt Gay kicked a 41-yard field goal for a 3-0 lead. Shough threw a 2-yard touchdown pass to Johnson, giving the Saints a 6-3 lead at the end of the first quarter, their first lead at the end of the opening period in Kellen Moore's 20 games as head coach. Gay kicked a 37-yard field goal to tie the score and Cousins threw a 3-yard touchdown pass to Michael Mayer to give Las Vegas a 13-6 lead. Shough's 3-yard touchdown pass to Fant tied the score, and Gay's 25-yard field goal gave the Raiders a 16-13 halftime lead. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vikings slide past Buccaneers, who lose Baker Mayfield
item.description: Myles Price had an 86-yard punt return for a touchdown, and the Minnesota Vikings held on for a 23-16 win over the host Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Myles Price had an 86-yard punt return for a touchdown, and the Minnesota Vikings held on for a 23-16 win over the host Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday afternoon. Kyler Murray completed 15 of 29 passes for 168 yards, one touchdown and one interception for Minnesota (3-0). Jordan Addison had 90 receiving yards and a score. Baker Mayfield completed 17 of 34 passes for 217 yards, one touchdown and one interception for Tampa Bay (0-3) before being injured. Ted Hurst III caught the Buccaneers' lone touchdown. Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel intercepted Mayfield on Tampa Bay's last-ditch effort on fourth-and-13. Mayfield was hit on the play and stayed down as teammates kneeled around him. He clutched his throwing hand as he walked off the field and has a dislocated thumb, according to coach Todd Bowles. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels was in for Tampa Bay's last possession and didn't complete any of his three throws, including an interception by Minnesota's Isasiah Rodgers on the final-play 'Hail Mary' throw. Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson injured his left ankle during the second quarter and did not return. He finished the game with two receptions for 32 yards. The Vikings opened the scoring with Will Reichard's 54-yard field goal on their first possession. After a defensive stop, Minnesota made it 10-0 with 8:43 remaining in the first quarter. Price fielded a punt at the Vikings' 14-yard line, weaved through several Buccaneers players and sprinted down the right sideline for an 86-yard touchdown. Tampa Bay cut the deficit to 10-7 on the next possession. Hurst got open across the middle, caught a pass from Mayfield and ran untouched into the end zone for a 40-yard score and his first career touchdown. A 28-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin evened the score at 10. The Vikings finished the first-half scoring with a 41-yard touchdown pass from Murray to Addison to regain a 17-10 lead. Tampa Bay tallied the only points of the third quarter. McLaughlin made a 38-yarder to bring the Buccaneers within 17-13. Another Buccaneers field goal trimmed the deficit to 17-16 with 9:02 remaining. Reichard came up big with his right leg to increase the Vikings' lead to 20-16 with 3:10 to go. He booted a 56-yard field goal to make it a four-point game. Minnesota made it 23-16 on Reichard's 43-yard field goal with 33 seconds left. -Field Level Media

item.title: 49ers finish off high-scoring win over Cardinals to remain perfect
item.description: Brock Purdy threw for 297 yards and four touchdowns as the San Francisco 49ers built a 17-point third-quarter lead before holding off a rally by the Arizona Cardinals for a 36-30 win on Sunday in Santa Clara, Calif.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brock Purdy threw for 297 yards and four touchdowns as the San Francisco 49ers built a 17-point third-quarter lead before holding off a rally by the Arizona Cardinals for a 36-30 win on Sunday in Santa Clara, Calif. Purdy completed 15 of 27 passes, including 10 and 20-yard strikes to George Kittle that kept Arizona at bay. Christian McCaffrey added 75 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries for San Francisco (3-0), which outgained Arizona 437-365 despite owning possession for just 21:16. Jacoby Brissett hit 38 of 52 attempts for 280 yards and two scores for Arizona (1-2), which dropped its second straight game after a season-opening win at the Los Angeles Chargers. The Cardinals got 90 yards on 21 carries from rookie Jeremiyah Love but hurt themselves with mistakes. Arizona was penalized 10 times for 86 yards and settled for field goals on two of its five trips inside the 49ers' 20-yard line. San Francisco initiated scoring in an unusual manner at the 8:26 mark of the first quarter. Purdy hit Mike Evans for a 2-yard gain and Evans lateraled to Deebo Samuel, who lugged it 80 more yards for a 7-0 lead. Purdy and Evans hooked up for a more conventional touchdown, a 23-yard pass to start the second quarter that made it 14-0. Evans left later in the half with a rib injury and was joined on the sidelines by left tackle Trent Williams (stinger). Chad Ryland converted field goals of 26 and 41 yards later in the second quarter for the Cardinals, but Eddy Pineiro bombed a 57-yarder as time expired for a 17-6 halftime lead. McCaffrey scored on a 1-yard plunge at the 11:07 mark of the third quarter to make it 23-6 before Arizona started its comeback. Brissett found Michael Wilson for a 5-yard touchdown pass with 3:02 left in the third. Love scored on a 1-yard run with 13:06 left in the game to draw the Cardinals within 23-20. After Kittle's first score, Brissett snuck over from the 1 with 2:51 remaining. Kittle's wide-open grab of a Purdy play-action pass put the Niners back up by nine with 1:31 to go. Ryland hit a 49-yard field goal with 34 seconds on the clock, but Samuel recovered the ensuing onside kick to seal the result. --Field Level Media

item.title: PepsiCo will invest $1 billion in Colombia over next five years, president says
item.description: PepsiCo will invest $1 billion in Colombia over the next five years, the South American nation's President Abelardo De La Espriella said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Nelson Bocanegra
item.content:encoded: PepsiCo (PEP.O) will invest $1 billion in Colombia over the next five years, the South American nation's President Abelardo De La Espriella said on Sunday. The investments will be aimed at expanding production, modernizing operations and strengthening distribution in the country, the president added. “Confidence is demonstrated through investment. This commitment will boost employment, support more than 2,000 farmers and strengthen Colombia’s small shopkeepers,” De La Espriella wrote on X. The announcement follows a weeklong visit to New York by Colombian Vice President José Manuel Restrepo and the country’s economic team, during which they met with more than 100 corporate and capital markets investors.

item.title: UK's Healey puts defence in focus for reindustrialisation push
item.description: British finance minister John Healey will put his support firmly behind firms investing in defence on Monday, part of what he will describe as a new industrialisation drive to try to spur the nation's anaemic economic growth.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey will put his support firmly behind firms investing in defence on Monday, part of what he will describe as a new industrialisation drive to try to spur the nation's anaemic economic growth. In his first speech to the governing Labour Party's annual conference as finance minister, Healey will aim to put flesh on the bones of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's pledge to reindustrialise Britain when he became the nation's seventh leader in a decade in July. Healey, who [USN:L8N42J0TA TEXT:"resigned as defence minister"] under former Prime Minister Keir Starmer over what he felt was inadequate spending on defence, will say a "new age of industrialisation" will see British firms deliver multi-billion pound defence projects, such as three new floating docks for submarines in Clyde in Scotland. "By backing British shipyards, we are not only boosting national security but also securing resilience in the industries that will drive growth today while building the capabilities the country needs for the future," Healey said in a statement. Burnham has pledged to meet a NATO target of increasing the core defence budget to 3.5% of GDP by 2035. BURNHAM WANTS REINDUSTRIALISATION TO CREATE JOBS The announcement is a taste of what Healey hopes to signal with his speech — that Burnham's government hopes the route to boosting growth and reducing unemployment, and the welfare bill, will stem from new jobs created by investments in sectors such as defence. At a conference aimed at [USN:L6N45J04E TEXT:"firing up Labour members"] and lawmakers with a message of hope, the new government also has a difficult task in navigating competing pressures — Burnham has promised to offer the public breathing space from cost-of-living pressures, but there is a cost to that. With conflict in the Middle East impacting energy costs and government finances tight ahead of [USN:L8N44P1EA TEXT:"Healey's first budget"] on October 28, Britain's new finance minister has little room to manoeuvre. On defence, his government also faces the need to fill a £4.7 billion ($6.2 billion) gap in its Defence Investment Plan, a blueprint some military experts say does not go far enough in meeting Britain's promise to increase defence spending. Healey has as yet not set out whether the government will reach defence spending of 3% of GDP by 2030 — a target he wanted but failed to persuade Starmer to sign up to, part of the reason he quit as defence minister. Burnham's new defence minister Wes Streeting said defence would drive Britain's reindustrialisation. "Defence spending should make Britain stronger in every sense," Streeting said. "That means backing British by buying British wherever our industry can deliver." ($1 = 0.7548 pounds)

item.title: Where will Fed tightening hit hardest in Asia?
item.description: As the US monetary tightening cycle gets underway, Asian markets face a formidable headwind, yet the structural impact will diverge sharply by country and sector.
item.dc:creator: Manishi Raychaudhuri
item.content:encoded: As the US monetary tightening cycle gets underway, Asian markets face a formidable headwind, yet the structural impact will diverge sharply by country and sector. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh announced on September 16 that the U.S. central bank was [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"hiking its benchmark interest rate"] by 25 basis points. But even more importantly, the Fed signalled that further increases could be coming to help combat inflation that has been above the 2% target for over five years. Fed officials’ views, encapsulated in the so-called “dot plot”, indicate that [USN:FOMGKEM2Z TEXT:"one more rate hike"] is likely this year. Markets, meanwhile, are expecting as many as [USN:L6N45D0VX TEXT:"three more rate hikes"] through the middle of next year. This hawkish shift in monetary policy is expected to affect Asian economies and financial markets through several interconnected channels, including by spurring capital outflows, weakening domestic currencies and bumping up inflationary pressures. But the effects should be far from uniform across the region. CAPITAL CRUNCH Higher US yields can draw global investors to dollar-denominated assets, leading to capital flight from emerging Asian markets. During the first 15 years of this century, US Treasury yields plummeted to ultra-low levels, especially following the global financial crisis of 2009-09. This triggered an avalanche of foreign capital into Asian equities. However, that began to change during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, only to worsen following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine , which compounded inflationary pressures and helped push rates higher. But it was the onset of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran this year that truly saw foreign investment flows into Asia collapse. Driven by US 10-year yields hovering at 4–5%, estimated monthly foreign-equity outflows reached a record $192 billion through September 25 — far eclipsing the previous 2025 peak of $45 billion, based on data from Asian stock exchanges. Predictably, many Asian currencies weakened significantly against the dollar during this period. Economies with current account deficits — such as India , Indonesia and the Philippines — were hit the hardest, as they rely heavily on foreign investments to finance their trade shortfalls. Meanwhile, the currencies of economies running current account surpluses, like China and South Korea, have appreciated. Obviously, other factors are at play here, especially in China, which doesn’t have a freely floating currency, but the pattern still holds. All of this suggests that if US interest rates continue to rise, the currencies of deficit economies could continue to slide further. INFLATION PANIC Depreciating local currencies typically fuel imported inflation. In the current episode, this dynamic is amplifying many other domestic price pressures impacting Asian economies, including the global energy supply shock and the El Nino weather pattern. Deficit countries in Asia with weak currencies are, unsurprisingly, seeing some of the highest levels of inflation. At the end of August, inflation stood at 4.8% in India, 3.2% in Indonesia, and 6.1% in the Philippines. These countries have also already notched multiple rate hikes this year. Since May, Bank Indonesia has [USN:L4N43M0IR TEXT:"hiked rates three times"] by 100 basis points cumulatively, while the Philippines' central bank has done so [USN:P8N415028 TEXT:"three times"] since April for a combined increase of 75 basis points. China, Taiwan and Malaysia remain Asia's notable inflation exceptions. This reflects weak domestic demand in China, while [USN:L4N44Z05L TEXT:"Taiwan"] and [USN:P8N3UE03Y TEXT:"Malaysia"] have enjoyed relatively stable exchange rates and tariff cuts, meaning pressure on their central banks to hike rates is virtually non-existent. SOME LOSE, SOME WIN Equity market valuations are also at risk across the region. Over the past decade, three instances of rising yields in Asia have been accompanied by declines in forward price-to-earnings (PE) multiples in various Asian equity markets, as rising discount rates have mechanically dragged down valuations. In the present episode, as the average 10-year yield in Asia rose from 3.4% in late October 2025 to 4.2% in late September, the 12-month forward PE multiple for the FactSet Asia Market Index declined from 16.7 times to 12.5 times. This trend could clearly worsen if US rates rise more than markets currently expect. Different sectors should react differently, however. “Long duration” equities – meaning companies whose value primarily resides far out in the future – obviously tend to see their valuations fall more due to the rising cost of capital. Technology often falls in this category. It’s unsurprising, therefore, that the PE multiples of the South Korean and Taiwanese markets – which are dominated by tech giants like Samsung (005930.KS) , SK Hynix (000660.KS) and TSMC (2330.TW) – have declined the most during the latest US yield surge. Soaring interest rates also jeopardize sectors dependent on high leverage or credit-driven demand. This hits capital-intensive industries like real estate and utilities facing higher refinancing costs, alongside consumer discretionary stocks constrained by tighter household borrowing. The most leveraged markets are the Philippines, Thailand and China, which had net debt-to-equity ratios in 2025 of 118%, 105% and 86% respectively, according to FactSet. Banks and insurers, on the other hand, are usually the winners during global rate tightening cycles. For banks, lending rates typically outpace deposit rates, boosting net interest margins. That was evident in the 2022–23 cycle, when the average net interest margin for Hong Kong's top 10 banks climbed from 1.41% to 1.65%. Insurance companies, meanwhile, can keep investing their new premium income in progressively higher-yielding bonds as rates rise, typically boosting their profitability. Markets with heavy financial weightings according to FactSet — led by Singapore at 47% of the market, Hong Kong at 32%, Malaysia at 31%, and India at 26% — stand to benefit the most from these dynamics dynamic. As rising capital costs reshuffle Asia’s economic deck, a sharp line is being drawn between resilient, low-inflation Asian economies and those burdened by heavy deficits and spiralling inflation. That line could deepen in the coming months. (The views expressed here are those of Manishi Raychaudhuri , the founder and CEO of Emmer Capital Partners Ltd and the former head of Asia-Pacific Equity Research at BNP Paribas Securities.) item.title: D-backs, eliminated earlier in the day, fall to Padres
item.description: Gavin Sheets homered and Freddy Fermin knocked in three runs as the San Diego Padres tuned up for their National League wild-card series by stopping the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks 9-4 on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Gavin Sheets homered and Freddy Fermin knocked in three runs as the San Diego Padres tuned up for their National League wild-card series by stopping the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks 9-4 on Sunday afternoon. San Diego (91-71), which opens its best-of-three series Tuesday night against the visiting Chicago Cubs, snapped a 4-4 tie with three runs in the bottom of the seventh. Fermin capped it with a two-run single. Arizona (86-76) was eliminated from postseason contention when Philadelphia completed a 7-3 win over Tampa Bay around the same time Jake Cronenworth drew a bases-loaded walk to push home the go-ahead run in the seventh. Griffin Canning (5-9) got the win despite allowing three runs in the top of the seventh that pulled the Diamondbacks even. Justin Martinez (3-1) was charged with the loss after issuing four straight one-out walks in the seventh. Neither starter factored in the decision. Arizona's Michael Soroka pitched 4 2/3 innings, allowing three hits and three runs with two walks and four strikeouts. The Padres' Randy Vasquez went six innings, permitting three hits and a run while walking none and striking out two. Manny Machado knocked in the game's first run in the bottom of the third with a two-out single that scored Sung-Mun Song. Machado got two at-bats in an attempt to hit his 400th career homer but was replaced after his single. Sheets' 17th homer of the year doubled the lead in the fourth and Ty France grounded an RBI single in the fifth for a 3-0 advantage. The Diamondbacks got on the board in the sixth via Ketel Marte's single that scored Jordan Lawlar. After Fermin doubled home a run in the San Diego sixth, Arizona tied the game in its half of the seventh. Corbin Carroll ripped an RBI double, followed by run-scoring singles from Tim Tawa and Lars Nootbaar. However, the Padres regained command in their half of the seventh and added insurance in the eighth on Austin Hays' two-run single. San Diego won seven straight series to end the regular season, going 18-4. --Field Level Media

item.title: Mariners win, hand Angels 100th loss for first time
item.description: Logan Gilbert pitched four-plus hitless innings and struck out eight as the Seattle Mariners defeated the visiting Los Angeles Angels 7-3 Sunday afternoon in the season finale.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Logan Gilbert pitched four-plus hitless innings and struck out eight as the Seattle Mariners defeated the visiting Los Angeles Angels 7-3 Sunday afternoon in the season finale. Jose Siri homered for the Angels, who suffered their franchise-record 100th loss of the season. They had been the lone active MLB team to never have had that many defeats. Gilbert didn't allow a baserunner until walking Moises Ballesteros leading off the fifth. Gilbert was then pulled by manager Dan Wilson to a standing ovation from the crowd at T-Mobile Park. Gilbert struck out the side in the first inning to reach 200 strikeouts for the season. It was the second time he reached the milestone and he became just the fourth pitcher in franchise history to do so multiple times, following Randy Johnson (seven), Felix Hernandez (six) and Mark Langston (four). The Mariners (76-86) struck first in the second inning. Cole Young reached on a one-out bunt down the third-base line and advanced to third on Jhonny Pereda's double to left that fell just in front of a diving Wade Meckler. Young scored on Weston Wilson's groundout to third. Seattle extended its lead in the third. Randy Arozarena was hit by a pitch from Yusei Kikuchi (1-7), a former Mariner, and Dominic Canzone singled to left. Cal Raleigh grounded a single down the right-field line, scoring Arozarena and sending Canzone to third. After Julio Rodriguez popped out, Canzone scored on Josh Naylor's groundout to second to make it 3-0. The Angels got on the board in the sixth. Bryce Teodosio led off with a single to right and Zach Neto walked against Eduard Bazardo (4-4), who was replaced by Hoby Milner. Jose Siri moved both runners over with a sacrifice bunt and Teodosio scored on Vaughn Grissom's sac fly to right. The Mariners answered with three unearned runs in the bottom of the inning off Trevor Martin. Young drew a one-out walk off Trevor Martin and Pereda singled to center. Young scored on a throwing error by Angels third baseman Denzer Guzman. With two outs, Arozarena hit a two-run double just over the outstretched glove of leaping left fielder Siri. The Angels scored in the eighth as Neto drew a leadoff walk against Troy Taylor and Siri went deep to left. The Mariners got their last run in the eighth as Leo Rivas and Michael Arroyo singled and, after a double play, Rivas scored on a wild pitch. Kikuchi gave up three runs on six hits over five innings, with one walk and seven strikeouts. --Field Level Media

item.title: Dodgers notch 100th win, knock off Giants in 10 innings
item.description: Andy Pages capped a four-run 10th inning with a three-run home run Sunday afternoon, and the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers beat San Francisco 5-1 in the final game of longtime Giants broadcaster Mike Krukow's career, earning their 100th win of the season
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Andy Pages capped a four-run 10th inning with a three-run home run Sunday afternoon, and the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers beat San Francisco 5-1 in the final game of longtime Giants broadcaster Mike Krukow's career, earning their 100th win of the season With Krukow working overtime as his postgame retirement ceremony was delayed, the Dodgers (100-62) took the lead in the 10th when Alex Call's two-out double off the left field fence drove in automatic runner Miguel Rojas. The Giants (65-97) then elected to walk Max Muncy, before Pages foiled that strategy by driving a pitch by Duncan Davitt (0-1) into the left field bleachers for a 5-1 lead on his 23rd home run of the season. Alex Vesia (3-1), whose perfect ninth sent the game into the 10th, was credited with the win, which allows the Dodgers to take a three-game winning streak into their National League Division Series opener next Saturday. Los Angeles' bid for a third straight World Series title will begin at home against either the Atlanta Braves or Philadelphia Phillies in a best-of-5 series. Both teams treated the finale as a bullpen game, then proceeded to exhaust much of their supply of arms. The Giants' only run came off Dodgers starter Jack Dreyer in the second when Scott Bandura's two-out single plated Shay Whitcomb, who had walked and stolen second. Dreyer was lifted after two innings, having allowed two hits. He struck out two. Justin Wrobleski, Roki Sasaki, Edwin Diaz, Bobby Miller, Vesia and Phillips shut out the Giants on just three hits over the final eight innings. The Dodgers took advantage of a Jonah Cox fielding error to draw even in the fourth. Muncy's double then set up a sacrifice fly by Pages off Sam Hentges. Carson Seymour got the start for the Giants and threw a 1-2-3 first inning. In losing for the fifth straight time to end the season, San Francisco used 10 pitchers, none for more than five outs. A majority of the changes were made after manager Tony Vitello was ejected in the third for having disputed a no-swing call on the Dodgers' Mookie Betts. Muncy and Tommy Edman each had two hits for the Dodgers, who finished the regular season 6-1 in extra-inning games. --Field Level Media
