item.title: Oil heads higher as US-Iran peace talks in stalemate
item.description: Brent crude futures rose to $106.14 a barrel.
item.dc:creator: Florence Tan
item.content:encoded: Oil prices rebounded more than 1% on Monday after US President Donald Trump rejected a [USN:L6N45J004 TEXT:"peace deal"] from Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, keeping tensions in the Middle East elevated. Brent crude futures rose $1.32, or 1.27%, to $105.64 a barrel by 0036 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $93.11 a barrel, up 70 cents, or 0.76%. Iran announced a peace proposal last week at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators. Trump said on Saturday he rejected the plan, but told Axios in a phone interview on Sunday that he expected US negotiators to engage in more talks this week. "Geopolitical risks remain elevated, as the Houthis and Iran continued their attacks on Saudi Arabia, leaving regional supply flows vulnerable," ANZ analysts said in a note. Yemen's Saudi-led coalition said early on Saturday it had [USN:L1N45I00U TEXT:"intercepted"] two ballistic missiles and two drones launched by the Iran-backed Houthis towards the kingdom. Brent edged up 0.4% last week but WTI lost 7.9% on concerns that the US may ban diesel exports to ease record prices which could [USN:L6N45G0YB TEXT:"curb"] US refining output. "Refined oil products remain a pressure point, with record US diesel prices intensifying inflation risks and prompting renewed debate over potential export curbs," ANZ analysts said. Any restriction on US diesel exports would tighten supply outside the US, with European prices reacting to the prospect of reduced American supply, they added. Meanwhile, [USN:L1N45J07E TEXT:"crude oil exports"] from key Middle East producers rebounded in September to 12.8 million barrels per day, the highest since the war started in February, preliminary data from Kpler showed on Monday, as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates boosted exports. The rebound came following a recovery in shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, which were set to hit about 7.4 million bpd this month, the data showed, as Saudi Arabia diverted exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu to its eastern Ras Tanura port following attacks that damaged its East-West pipeline.

item.title: Bill Gates se suma a los llamados sobre medidas de protección frente a la IA
item.description: La inteligencia artificial requiere medidas de protección que vayan más allá de la autorregulación, afirmó el cofundador de Microsoft, Bill Gates, en una entrevista emitida el domingo, en la que pidió que se apruebe una ley en el Congreso.
item.dc:creator: Idrees Ali, Trevor Hunnicutt
item.content:encoded: La inteligencia artificial requiere medidas de protección que vayan más allá de la autorregulación, afirmó el cofundador de Microsoft, Bill Gates, en una entrevista emitida el domingo, en la que pidió que se apruebe una ley en el Congreso. "Es necesario que las fuerzas del orden y los políticos se sumen al debate sobre cómo deben ser esas medidas de seguridad y ese control", afirmó Gates en una entrevista grabada para el programa Meet the Press de la NBC. "Y eso tiene que ser obligatorio". Se ha producido una repentina oleada de apoyo a la intervención federal después de que OpenAI anunciara en julio que un agente autónomo de IA se rebeló durante una prueba de seguridad y pirateó otra empresa, eludiendo el control humano. Gates se sumó a ese coro, afirmando que el Gobierno debe intervenir. "Nadie cree que la autorregulación sea suficiente", afirmó. En una inusual muestra de unidad, los directores ejecutivos de las empresas rivales Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind (GOOGL.O) , de Google, Microsoft (MSFT.O) y xAI han pedido que se frene el desarrollo de sistemas de IA cada vez más capaces. Sin embargo, el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, y otros detractores de una mayor regulación de la IA sostienen que las nuevas restricciones gubernamentales no harían más que dar ventaja a China en la revolución de la IA. Trump ha desestimado las peticiones de nuevas leyes sobre la IA. Gates argumentó que las medidas de protección no supondrían un obstáculo drástico para el sector y que los riesgos de no aplicarlas son reales. "No es ningún infundio en absoluto", declaró a la NBC. Gates ha manifestado que quiere reunirse con Trump para hablar sobre la IA. "Espero que, dada mi trayectoria profesional en este campo, el hecho de que yo explique lo singular y diferente que es esto y lo preocupado que estoy sirva para complementar lo que él está escuchando de otras personas", afirmó Gates. Se espera que el director ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, cene con Trump el domingo, según una fuente familiarizada con el asunto. Axios ya había informado de la cena. Ni Anthropic ni la Casa Blanca respondieron de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. "El presidente Trump ha sido claro: Estados Unidos liderará el mundo en materia de superinteligencia, al tiempo que protegerá a los consumidores estadounidenses", afirmó un funcionario de la Casa Blanca. Las advertencias sobre los riesgos de la IA no son nuevas. Sin embargo, este mes han cobrado mayor urgencia después de que investigadores de los principales laboratorios de IA asignaran tanto un plazo como una probabilidad a esas preocupaciones. El exinvestigador de Anthropic Jacob Coxon advirtió de que la IA podría acabar con todos nosotros a finales de esta década, lo que llevó a los legisladores estadounidenses a reclamar nuevas normas para regular esta tecnología. Evan Hubinger, responsable de ciencia de alineación de Anthropic, se hizo eco de la advertencia de Coxon y afirmó que había más de un 10% de probabilidades de que se produjera un suceso de este tipo en la próxima década. Algunos responsables políticos han propuesto imponer un "interruptor de emergencia" que permitiría a las autoridades federales detener los modelos de IA. Gates afirmó que, aunque no se oponía a algún tipo de interruptor de emergencia, éste no sería suficiente si no se implementaran también otras medidas de seguridad. Estados Unidos y China acordaron iniciar un diálogo sobre la IA tras la reciente visita del presidente Xi Jinping a Washington.

item.title: Pirates tame Tigers to secure first winning mark since 2018
item.description: Jared Jones pitched four inning of one-hit ball and Konnor Griffin led off the game with a solo home run and drove in two runs to lead the Pirates to a 4-2 win over the host Tigers on Sunday in Detroit, Mich.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jared Jones pitched four inning of one-hit ball and Konnor Griffin led off the game with a solo home run and drove in two runs to lead the Pirates to a 4-2 win over the host Tigers on Sunday in Detroit, Mich. Griffin's solo homer was the sixth of his rookie season and first of two hits and helped Pittsburgh (82-80) secure its first winning record since 2018 and only its second since it last made the postseason in 2015. The Tigers (76-86) finished with a losing record after advancing to the American League Division Series each of the past two seasons. Jones was not eligible for the win after exiting the game before the fifth, but struck out five and did not walk a batter. Jones finished 5-6 with a 3.72 ERA in 21 starts after returning from elbow surgery in late May. He capped a stellar September in which he went 3-0 with a 0.93 ERA, allowing only three earned runs in 29 innings (five starts). Rookie River Ryan (0-1) made his second career start and allowed two runs on three hits, struck out three and walked two over 1 1/3 innings. Pirates closer Mason Montgomery picked up his 18th save, striking out two in a perfect ninth inning. Jake Mangum extended the Pirates' lead to 2-0 with an RBI single in the second to score Spencer Horwitz, who led off the inning with a walk. Billy Cook doubled with two outs in the fourth to drive in Nick Gonzales and scored on Griffin's RBI single to put Pittsburgh up 4-0. Detroit finally broke through in the bottom of the seventh on back-to-back solo home runs by AL Rookie of the Year candidate Kevin McGonigle and Eduardo Valencia off reliever Antwone Kelly. McGonigle led the Tigers with two of their three hits. Lake Bachar (2-4) relieved Kelly and struck out Brett Callihan and Jace Jung, although Jung reached first on a wild pitch on strike three. Bachar then struck out Zach McKinstry to end the inning. He finished with four of 13 strikeouts by Pittsburgh's pitchers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Season-finale loss to Twins knocks Rangers out of playoff race
item.description: Josh Bell hit a two-run home run and drove in three to lead the host Minnesota Twins to a 6-4 season-ending win over the Texas Rangers on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Josh Bell hit a two-run home run and drove in three to lead the host Minnesota Twins to a 6-4 season-ending win over the Texas Rangers on Sunday. The loss eliminated the Rangers (80-82) from the American League West title race and the playoffs. Texas needed to beat the Twins and the Astros to lose to the Athletics. Starter Dean Kremer (5-5) gave up three hits and one run in seven innings for the Twins (77-85). The right-hander didn't issue any walks and struck out four over 74 pitches. Kremer yielded a home run to Danny Jansen, but did not allow another Texas runner past first base. Rangers starter Mackenzie Gore allowed one hit and one run in 2 1/3 innings. The left-hander walked one and did not have a strikeout in 25 pitches. The Rangers used six pitchers in an attempt to stay in the playoff hunt. Chase Silseth (3-4) took the loss when he gave up Bell's home run. The Twins took the early lead when Luke Keaschall led off the first with a walk, went to second on a Kaelen Culpepper single and scored on a Bell sacrifice fly. The Rangers tied it in the third with Jansen's leadoff home run. Keaschall started another rally in the third when he was hit by a pitch with one out. Bell made it 3-1 Twins by smashing a two-out home run to right. Minnesota extended the lead in the fifth when Walker Jenkins led off with a single. Keaschall walked and Bell loaded the bases with a one-out walk. Ryan Jeffers made it three straight walks to bring home Jenkins for a 4-1 lead. Kody Clemens made it 5-1 by singling in Keaschall. A.J. Minter relieved Kremer to start the eighth and pinch hitter Elias Diaz greeted him with a leadoff home run to left to cut Minnesota's lead to 5-2. The Twins added an insurance run in the eighth when Royce Lewis led off with a home run to center. Texas cut the lead to two when Corey Seager hit a two-run home run in the ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: US roar back to beat Internationals for 11th consecutive Presidents Cup win
item.description: Jacob Bridgeman clinched the winning point as the United States rallied to beat the International Team 17-13 and retain the Presidents Cup near Chicago on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Rory Carroll
item.content:encoded: Jacob Bridgeman clinched the winning point as the United States rallied to beat the International Team 17-13 and retain the Presidents Cup near Chicago on Sunday. Bridgeman beat Australia's Min Woo Lee 1-up to give the Americans the 15-1/2 points required to secure the trophy, completing a final-day turnaround after the US began Sunday trailing 10-1/2 to 7-1/2. The victory was the United States' 11th consecutive Presidents Cup title. The Americans improved their overall record in the biennial team event against an International side drawn from outside Europe to 14-1-1. The US needed eight points from 12 singles matches and received wins from Cameron Young, Justin Thomas, Scottie Scheffler, Chris Gotterup, Collin Morikawa, Patrick Cantlay and Jackson Koivun before Bridgeman delivered the decisive point in his tournament debut. 'BEST GOLFERS IN THE WORLD' "I saw a bunch of guys who didn't want to quit on each other," US team captain Brandt Snedeker said. "I saw the best golfers in the world come out here on a mission... I'm just so damn proud." Bridgeman said the emotions he had kept in check throughout the day spilled out after he sank the decisive 3-foot putt at Medinah Country Club's No. 3 Course outside Chicago. "To let it out on the last hole was pretty sweet," he said. Xander Schauffele later won his match and Russell Henley halved his, extending the final margin to four points. The Internationals had been in position to claim their first outright Presidents Cup victory since 1998, and early singles wins by South Koreans Tom Kim and Sungjae Im moved them within striking distance of the title. But the Americans took control as the day wore on, while the International side struggled on the greens. CANTLAY DRILLS 57-FOOT PUTT Cantlay provided one of the defining moments when he holed a 57-foot putt from off the 16th green in his match against Australia's Adam Scott. Cantlay pumped his fist as the home crowd erupted into chants of "USA! USA!" before he closed out the match on the next hole. Morikawa then won a tight, back-and-forth match against Japan's Hideki Matsuyama to put the United States ahead 13-1/2 to 12-1/2. Koivun, 21, beat South Korea's Si Woo Kim to move the Americans within a point of victory before Bridgeman sealed the comeback. "It has been such a cool learning experience," said Koivun, who went undefeated in his Presidents Cup debut. "And to come out on top after a large deficit coming into today is a feeling I can't explain," he said. "I'm just grateful for the trust the captain put in me." TRUMP, WOODS PRAISE US TEAM The day began with US President Donald Trump addressing players from the first tee, and ended with Snedeker crediting him with helping inspire the Americans' comeback. "The American team was unbelievable, it was a big, big win," Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland. "You witnessed a very historic event today. It was actually, in terms of sport and in terms of golf, and in terms of our country, it was a great win." Former US captain Tiger Woods also praised the Americans' final-day rally. "What a comeback!" Woods posted on social media. "Congrats to Team USA on an incredible Presidents Cup victory. They needed all the matchups to go their way today, and they got it done. Great team win."

item.title: Alex Bregman stars for Cubs in neutral-site win over Red Sox
item.description: Alex Bregman went 4-for-4 with two home runs and four RBIs against his former team to help the Chicago Cubs wrap up the regular season by defeating the Boston Red Sox 6-2 Sunday in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alex Bregman went 4-for-4 with two home runs and four RBIs against his former team to help the Chicago Cubs wrap up the regular season by defeating the Boston Red Sox 6-2 Sunday in St. Petersburg, Fla. The game was scheduled to be played in Boston, but was moved to Tropicana Field because of the nor'easter that hit much of New England throughout the weekend. Both of Bregman's home runs came against Boston starter Tanner Houck, who made his first appearance on the mound since May 2025. Houck (0-1), who had Tommy John surgery last year, allowed three runs on four hits in three innings. Bregman, who spent the 2025 season with Boston, added an RBI double and a single in the victory. He also walked once. Braxton Garrett (1-1) limited Boston to a run on four hits in five innings of relief, and Colin Rea held Boston scoreless in the final two innings to earn his second save. The victory prevented Boston from sweeping the three-game series. The Red Sox (87-75) were held to five hits and were 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position. Adley Rutschman homered for the Red Sox. Bregman's first home run put the Cubs up 2-0 in the top of the first. Rutschman hit a solo home run in the bottom of the first to make it 2-1, and Boston tied the game when Nick Sogard scored on a fielder's choice in the bottom of the second. The Cubs (89-73) led 3-2 after Bregman hit his second home run in the third. It was his 28th home run of the season. Chicago extended its lead to 6-2 by adding three runs in the ninth. After Bregman's RBI double drove in Miguel Amaya, Gabriel Arias hit a sacrifice fly that allowed Tyrone Taylor to score and stretch Chicago's advantage to 5-2. Michael Conforto's double drove in Bregman with the game's final run. Both teams will be involved in Tuesday's wild-card round. Boston will open its series against the Yankees in New York, and Chicago will play at the San Diego Padres. --Field Level Media

item.title: Illinois DC Bobby Hauck out after Ohio State beatdown
item.description: Illinois defensive coordinator Bobby Hauck is out after a 42-19 loss at Ohio State on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Illinois defensive coordinator Bobby Hauck is out after a 42-19 loss at Ohio State on Saturday. Fighting Illini head coach Bret Bielema said Sunday that he met with Hauck before the scheduled team gathering at the request of his assistant coach. "Coach Hauck reached out to me early this morning and asked to meet ahead of our planned meeting time. We met and mutually agreed that a change in leadership was in the best interests of our defense," Bielema said. "Coach Hauck and I agreed this is the best path forward for our staff, and most important, our student-athletes. "... As with any turnover, we have prepared for this moment and we have a plan to move our program forward. We are communicating that plan internally to our staff and players today." Hauck said in a statement released by the program he "enjoyed being a part of the staff" and wished Illinois luck. Illinois dropped to No. 111 in total defense in the FBS, allowing 391 yards per game. By comparison, Notre Dame is No. 1 in total defense at 199.2 yards per game. There are 138 FBS programs. After a 14-7 first quarter, Illinois was outscored 28-12 by Ohio State the rest of the way to drop to 2-2 this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jacob Misiorowski makes Cy Young case as Brewers down Cardinals
item.description: Jacob Misiorowski strengthened his Cy Young case, allowing just two hits over five-plus scoreless innings, as the Milwaukee Brewers built momentum for the postseason with a 6-4 victory over the visiting St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jacob Misiorowski strengthened his Cy Young case, allowing just two hits over five-plus scoreless innings, as the Milwaukee Brewers built momentum for the postseason with a 6-4 victory over the visiting St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday. Milwaukee (103-59), which has clinched a first-round Wild Card bye and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs, closed with five consecutive wins to extend its franchise record for victories in a season. Milwaukee, the first team to win four consecutive NL Central titles, finished 35-17 against division rivals and went 18-6 in September. St. Louis (77-85) scored four runs in the eighth off Chad Patrick to pull within 6-4, capped by Leo Bernal's three-run homer. Shane Drohan got the final five outs for his second save. Misiorowski (16-5) allowed two singles in 5 1/3 innings, departing after striking out Jordan Walker in the sixth to end a 68-pitch outing, lowering his major league-leading ERA to 1.80. Misiorowski struck out five and walked two, giving him 252 strikeouts for the year. Misiorowski is the second Brewers pitcher to lead the league in ERA, joining Corbin Burnes (2021). Milwaukee bunched six singles off Andre Pallante in the first inning for a 3-0 lead. Garrett Mitchell, Jake Bauers and Jackson Chourio opened with consecutive singles for the first run. Brice Turang reached on a run-scoring infield single, giving him 100 RBIs for the season. Christian Yelich singled in another run. Gary Sanchez put the Brewers up 5-0 with one out in the third with his 12th home run following a leadoff single by Chourio. Chourio's RBI single in the fourth made it 6-0. St. Louis rallied in the eighth when Cesar Prieto triple to open and Pedro Pages walked. Prieto scored on Jordan Walker's fielder's choice grounder. Ivan Herrera walked and Bernal followed with his fifth homer. Pallante (12-9) allowed six runs on 10 hits in five innings, striking out four and walking one. St. Louis, which has not made the postseason since 2022 and has not won a playoff series since the NLDS in 2019, was 50-45 at the All-Star break, but went 27-40 the rest of the way. --Field Level Media

item.title: Iran-linked diesel price spike makes electric trucks cheaper than diesel in key EU markets, environmental group says
item.description: A surge in diesel prices linked to this year's Iran conflict has helped make electric trucks cheaper to own and operate than diesel models in six major European Union markets, which account for almost half of the bloc's new truck sales, according to an analysis by Brussels-based environmental advocacy group Transport & Environment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A surge in diesel prices linked to this year's Iran conflict has helped make electric trucks cheaper to own and operate than diesel models in six major European Union markets, which account for almost half of the bloc's new truck sales, according to an analysis by Brussels-based environmental advocacy group Transport & Environment. The report, published on Monday, found that electric trucks purchased in 2026 generate savings over five years of up to €100,000 ($113,910) in the Netherlands, €85,000 in Germany and €69,000 in Denmark compared with diesel vehicles In those markets, operators can recoup the initial price premium in around two years T&E said rising diesel prices following this year's Iran-linked oil price spike strengthened the business case for electrification Europe's electric truck transition has been slowed by high purchase prices and patchy charging infrastructure The report examined total cost of ownership in nine EU countries It found that electric trucks were already cheaper to operate than diesel models in the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Sweden, France and Belgium, markets accounting for 46% of EU heavy-truck registrations. Reuters [USN:L6N3ZY0KY TEXT:"reported"] earlier this year that European truckmakers such as Daimler Truck (DTGGe.DE) , Volvo Group (VOLVb.ST) and Traton's Scania were bracing for a wave of lower-cost Chinese competitors, with some Chinese electric trucks expected to be priced about 30% below comparable European models T&E estimated a Chinese-built electric truck costs about €210,000, versus €265,000 for a European equivalent. In Germany, operators could save an additional €34,000 over five years by choosing a Chinese-made electric truck. ($1 = 0.8779 euro)

item.title: Max Scherzer wins potential last start as Jays shut down Reds
item.description: In potentially his final career start, Max Scherzer struck out seven over seven-plus innings and the Toronto Blue Jays defeated the visiting Cincinnati Reds 5-1 Sunday afternoon in the teams' season finale.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: In potentially his final career start, Max Scherzer struck out seven over seven-plus innings and the Toronto Blue Jays defeated the visiting Cincinnati Reds 5-1 Sunday afternoon in the teams' season finale. The 42-year-old Scherzer (4-9) allowed one run, six hits and one walk to earn his 225th career win and boost his strikeout total to 3,557. He left to a standing ovation and hugs from manager John Schneider on the mound after walking Oswaldo Cabrera to lead off the eighth. Mason Fluharty replaced Scherzer. George Springer, who might have also played his last game, also received a standing ovation when he was replaced in the third after a leadoff double. Brandon Valenzuela hit a two-run home run for the Blue Jays (79-83) and Charles McAdoo added a solo shot in the rubber match of the three-game series. Scherzer received a long ovation before making his first pitch. He has yet to decide if he will pitch again next year. The 37-year-old Springer, whose six-year contract is expiring, was loudly cheered before he led off the home first as DH. Toronto took a 2-0 lead in the second against Cincinnati starter Brandon Williamson (5-5). Davis Schneider led off with a walk, then Valenzuela hit a 2-0 cutter to center for his ninth homer of the season. Carlos Jorge's glove came off on his leaping attempt at the wall. The Reds (75-87) scored once in the third. Cabrera doubled and scored when Jorge scooped a single to center. Toronto answered with two runs in the bottom of the third. Springer led off with a double to left that bounced past JJ Bleday. Sean Keys replaced Springer as a pinch runner. Brett Bateman singled, Kazuma Okamoto walked and McAdoo hit a sacrifice fly to right. Schneider's groundout to third made it 4-1. Williamson allowed four runs, four hits and three walks with three strikeouts in three innings. McAdoo hit his third homer of the season with two outs in the eighth against Carson Spiers. Toronto's Paul Sewald pitched around a double in the ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Marlins fend off Braves in season finale
item.description: Heriberto Hernandez and Griffin Conine slugged solo home runs, giving the host Miami Marlins a 5-3 win over the Atlanta Braves on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Heriberto Hernandez and Griffin Conine slugged solo home runs, giving the host Miami Marlins a 5-3 win over the Atlanta Braves on Sunday afternoon. For the Braves (94-68), it was their last game before the playoffs. The National League East champions will face the division rival Philadelphia Phillies in the wild-card round. It was the season finale for the Marlins (80-82), who won one more game than they did last year. Sandy Alcantara, Miami's ace starter, tossed a scoreless ninth inning for his third career save. It was a fitting end of the year for Alcantara, who threw both the first and last pitch of the season for Miami. Braves starter JR Ritchie (1-5) took the loss. He allowed seven hits, two walks and four runs in 5 2/3 innings. Miami starter Janson Junk left with a no-decision. He allowed three hits, one walk and one run in 4 2/3 innings, fanning five. Michael Petersen (4-4) earned the win with 1 1/3 hitless innings of relief. Mauricio Dubon ambushed Junk in the third inning, belting a first-pitch sweeper 385 feet to left for his 12th homer of the year. That 102-mph blast -- just over the glove of Hernandez -- gave Atlanta a 1-0 lead. Hernandez got even in the fourth as he smacked a 1-0 changeup over the fence in left-center, tying the score 1-1. It was Hernandez's team-high and career-high 25th homer of the season, and it traveled 395 feet with a 105-mph exit velocity. Hernandez also played a key role in the sixth inning by blistering a leadoff double to left-center at 107 mph. With two outs, Esteury Ruiz drove in Hernandez with the go-ahead run. Later in the inning, the Marlins added Jared Serna's two-run double down the third base line to make it 4-1. Working against reliever Calvin Faucher in the seventh, Atlanta closed its deficit to 4-3. Ha-Seong Kim walked to win a 10-pitch at-bat, and Brewer Hicklen lofted a bloop single to set up the rally. The Braves cashed in as DaShawn Keirsey Jr. hit an RBI groundout, and Dubon stroked an opposite-field, line-drive single to right for another run. The Marlins extended their lead to 5-3 in the bottom of the seventh on Conine's 415-foot homer to right. That had a 110-mph exit velocity. Alcantara did the rest in Miami's 2026 finale. --Field Level Media

item.title: Randal Grichuk, Brenton Doyle help White Sox beat Rockies
item.description: Randal Grichuk and Brenton Doyle smacked two-run home runs and Anthony Kay pitched five strong innings to boost the host Chicago White Sox to a 4-2 victory against the Colorado Rockies on Sunday to close the regular season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Randal Grichuk and Brenton Doyle smacked two-run home runs and Anthony Kay pitched five strong innings to boost the host Chicago White Sox to a 4-2 victory against the Colorado Rockies on Sunday to close the regular season. The White Sox (84-78) are set to visit the American League West champion, either Houston or Texas, on Tuesday in the opener of an AL wild-card series. Chicago on Thursday clinched its first playoff berth since 2021 but was eliminated from contention for an AL Central title with Saturday's loss to Colorado and a Cleveland victory at Kansas City. Colorado (58-104) finished with 100 losses for the fourth successive season. Chicago accomplished that dubious feat for three consecutive campaigns, including a major-league record 121 defeats in 2024, before regrouping this season. Colorado had baserunners in each of its five times at bat against Kay but only managed one run. The Rockies took a 1-0 lead in the third. Jordan Beck and Ezequiel Tovar singled to open the inning and advanced on a sacrifice bunt before Connor Norby hit an RBI sacrifice fly to score Beck. The White Sox grabbed the lead in the bottom half. Grichuk drove a two-run shot to left field against Rockies left-hander Kyle Freeland while Doyle connected three batters later to put Chicago ahead 4-1. Cole Carrigg reached Chicago reliever Trevor Richards for a solo homer with two out in the eighth. Freeland fell to 4-12 after pitching four innings of seven-hit, four-run ball with one hit batter and two strikeouts. He retired the first four Chicago hitters but struggled after that, finishing the season with a 6.65 ERA in 26 starts Kay (10-9) gave up one run and five hits in five innings with two walks and four strikeouts. His 10 victories extended a career high after Kay dealt with injuries and inconsistency during the first part of his career. He pitched in Japan the past two seasons before signing with the White Sox in December. Sam Antonacci had two hits for the White Sox, who finished 48-33 at Rate Field. The Rockies had 55 road losses compared to 49 at home. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vinnie Pasquantino (2 HRs), Royals edge Guardians in season finale
item.description: Vinnie Pasquantino's second solo homer of the day broke an eighth-inning tie and sent the Kansas City Royals to a 3-2 victory over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Vinnie Pasquantino's second solo homer of the day broke an eighth-inning tie and sent the Kansas City Royals to a 3-2 victory over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Sunday. With Cleveland's Austin Peterson (0-1) pitching in his fifth inning of his second major league game, Pasquantino led off the eighth by sending a 2-2 sinker well into the right field seats. Pasquantino also homered off Peterson in the fifth, while Jac Caglianone and Kyle Isbel each had two hits for the Royals (69-94), who ended a disappointing 2026 campaign by avoiding a sweep and winning for just the seventh time in the final 25 games. Kansas City starter Daniel Lynch IV allowed seven hits in two runs over a season-high 5 1/3 innings. Lucas Erceg yielded one hit in the ninth and earned his 13th save of the season. Daniel Schneeman and Jo Adell each homered and had two hits apiece for the Guardians (85-77), who rested key regulars Steven Kwan, Jose Ramirez and Brayan Rocchio one day after securing their third consecutive American League Central title. All-Star rookie starter Parker Messick gave up six hits and a walk in three innings, but only one run, for Cleveland, which earned a bye into the AL Division Series. This was just the second loss in the final 11 games for the Guardians. The Royals wasted no time getting to Messick. Maikel Garcia opened the bottom of the first inning with a walk, advanced to third on Caglianone's one-out double, then scored via a Salvador Perez single to left field. Cleveland tied the game in the third when Schneemann went deep over the right field fence in his first at-bat of the series. Pasquantino cleared the center field wall in the fifth for a 2-1 Kansas City edge. Adell tied it in the sixth with a one-out drive into the left-center-field fountains. Nate Pearson (3-4) pitched a scoreless two-thirds of an inning for the Royals, who went 41-40 at home. --Field Level Media

item.title: Week 3 SNF: Rams-Broncos Preview, Props, Prediction
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams travel to face the Denver Broncos on Sunday night in a big early-season matchup between 1-1 teams with aspirations of deep playoff runs.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Rams travel to face the Denver Broncos on Sunday night in a big early-season matchup between 1-1 teams with aspirations of deep playoff runs. The Rams are expected to be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for a second consecutive game, but the offense found its rhythm without him in a 28-6 rout of the New York Giants in Week 2. The Broncos, meanwhile, earned a come-from-behind win against Jacksonville to avoid dropping their first two games of the season. ODDS AND TRENDS The Rams are consensus 2.0-point favorites, although the line has moved to -1.5 at several sportsbooks, including BetRivers, Caesars, DraftKings and FanDuel. It has dipped to just 1.0 point at BetRivers, where the public has been more evenly split. The Broncos and Rams were not among the top five in any wagers related to game spreads or moneyline action. PROP PICKS --Rams WR Davante Adams Anytime TD (+115 at DraftKings): With Nacua out last week, Adams was the focus of the Giants' defense and still led the Rams with 10 targets and a pair of touchdowns. He'll draw a lot of attention from Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain on Sunday night, but that won't prevent Matthew Stafford from looking his way often. --Broncos QB Bo Nix 220+ Passing Yards (+111 at DraftKings): Nix has thrown for at least 242 yards in seven consecutive games against NFC opponents. He is coming off a 288-yard passing effort against Jacksonville after throwing for only 131 in the season opener. --Rams TE Jake Ferguson Under 3.5 Receptions (-154 at BetMGM): Ferguson also benefited from Nacua's absence in Week 2, catching six of his nine targets. He could be in line for another significant role in the passing game against the Broncos, but the Rams also utilize three tight ends in the passing game along with Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen. Ferguson had no catches and just one target in the season opener. KEY STAT ... OR COINCIDENCE? The Broncos have a nine-game winning streak against NFC opponents dating to their loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 1 of the 2024 season. "I think that's just by schedule, by chance," Nix said. "We've competed against some really good teams. We've had some close NFC matchups. One that I remember is last year, the Eagles. They gave us a challenge, and we had to come back, and same with the Giants." Interestingly, the Rams have rattled off eight straight victories against AFC opponents since losing to the Miami Dolphins in Week 10 of the 2024 season. ADAMS IN CHARGE Davante Adams could be without prolific Rams sidekick Puka Nacua for the second straight week, but the veteran wide receiver has learned you don't worry about things you can't control. Adams was a receiving machine in Week 2 and he will look for another stellar performance when Los Angeles visits the Denver Broncos on Sunday night. Adams stood tall against the Giants with eight receptions for 195 yards and two touchdowns. The yardage was the fourth-highest of his 13-year career and just 11 shy of his career high set in 2021 as a member of the Green Bay Packers. "He's an elite player," Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford said of Adams. "He did it all for us, and he's a guy that can do that. We understand that. We know it." Adams, 33, is in his second season with Los Angeles (1-1). The six-time Pro Bowler led the NFL with 14 touchdown receptions last season. The guy who caught passes from Aaron Rodgers in Green Bay for eight seasons certainly appreciates playing with someone like Stafford. The reigning NFL Most Valuable Player threw four touchdown passes against the Giants to move into sixth place in league history with 427 career touchdown passes. "Football is the greatest team sport that there is, and it's a beautiful game because it takes so many things in order for things to go right," said Adams, a three-time first-team All-Pro. "We can both (Stafford and Adams) be great players and go out there and have the right intentions every time, and it doesn't guarantee anything for you." Broncos four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II is ready for the challenges that come with defending Adams. "It's good battles, good competition," said Surtain, a two-time first-team All-Pro. "It's going to be another battle on Sunday. Looking forward to it." INJURY REPORT Rams: Nacua (hip) is listed as doubtful, and coach Sean McVay said this week that Nacua's injury could become more serious if rest doesn't heal it. "It's some of those things that can kind of be pre-hernia," McVay said Wednesday before emphasizing that Nacua does not have a hernia. "You err on the side of caution. Usually time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal. And then once you get to a certain point, then I think you feel pretty good moving forward." In addition to Nacua, safety Kamren Kinchens (hamstring) is doubtful and tight end Colby Parkinson (knee) is questionable. Inside linebacker Nate Landman (shoulder) carries no game designation despite being limited in practice Wednesday through Friday. Broncos: Denver had concerns at running back after J.K. Dobbins injured his hip against Jacksonville, but both he and backfield mate RJ Harvey (hamstring) practiced in full Thursday and Friday and were cleared to play. No. 3 running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) is out, and receiver Marvin Mims Jr. (foot) is questionable. PREDICTION: The Broncos are at home in an intriguing prime-time game. Despite Nix's solid box score against the Jaguars, he still has been inconsistent pushing the ball downfield early in the season. With Aaron Donald back in the mix of a ferocious defensive line, the Rams will control field position and set Stafford and company up with shorter fields. --Rams 27, Broncos 20 --Field Level Media

item.title: Phillies beat Rays to clinch final NL playoff spot in Game 162
item.description: Zack Wheeler pitched six strong innings and Kyle Schwarber drove in two runs as the Philadelphia Phillies clinched their fifth straight postseason berth with a 7-3 win over the visiting Tampa Bay Rays on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Zack Wheeler pitched six strong innings and Kyle Schwarber drove in two runs as the Philadelphia Phillies clinched their fifth straight postseason berth with a 7-3 win over the visiting Tampa Bay Rays on Sunday. Bryce Harper and Edmundo Sosa homered for Philadelphia (88-74), which had lost its previous four games by the combined score of 23-3. The Phillies finally showed signs of life in Game 162, and now they'll head to Atlanta to face the Braves in the National League wild-card round. Tampa Bay (98-64), which clinched the top seed in the American League playoffs before even arriving in Philadelphia, will face the winner of the first-round series between the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox. Nick Martinez (15-6) got the start for the Rays and allowed four runs and seven hits in 2 2/3 innings. Jonny DeLuca was the offensive star for Tampa Bay with a pair of home runs, giving him 11 on the season. Wheeler (14-5) yielded one run and five hits, striking out five without a walk. Bryson Stott went 3-for-3 for the Phillies. Philadelphia quickly jumped out to a 1-0 lead as Schwarber singled with one out in the first inning and scored on Stott's two-out double. The Phillies scored three more two-out runs in the second inning. J.T. Realmuto's RBI double snapped an 0-for-34 slump and made it 2-0. Trea Turner followed with a single and Schwarber knocked in two runs with a double off the wall in right field. Meanwhile, Wheeler held the Rays scoreless until DeLuca led off the fifth with a homer. Harper immediately got that run back with a leadoff blast in the bottom half. Stott followed with a double and came around to score on Brandon Marsh's sacrifice fly. Sosa tacked on an opposite-field solo shot on the very next pitch to make it 7-1. Alex McFarlane took over for Wheeler to start the seventh and gave up an opposite-field solo homer to DeLuca, as well as an RBI hit by Victor Mesa Jr. later in the frame. Jesus Luzardo, typically a key member of the Philadelphia rotation, pitched the eighth after missing the last three weeks with a sore shoulder. He needed only four pitches to record three outs. Jhoan Duran retired the Rays in order in the ninth, sparking a subdued on-field celebration by the Phillies. --Field Level Media

item.title: Boston-bound Delta flight makes emergency landing in Portugal due to smoke in cabin
item.description: A Delta flight from Barcelona to Boston made an emergency landing on Sunday afternoon in Porto, Portugal, the airline operator said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Delta flight from Barcelona to Boston made an emergency landing on Sunday afternoon in Porto, Portugal, the airline operator said. Flight DL251 was diverted to Porto following a reported mechanical issue and landed there safely, the company said. Flight data from tracking service Flightradar24 suggested the plane left Barcelona at 3:15 p.m. (1315 GMT) and landed in Porto at 5:45 p.m. (1645 GMT). Eight passengers who had been onboard the Airbus A330 plane were treated on the tarmac at Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport in Porto while three others were taken to hospital for treatment, a spokesperson for Portugal's emergency and civil protection authority told Reuters by phone. The forced landing was due to smoke in the cabin, the Portuguese spokesperson added.

item.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 to end fractious weekend with Nations League win
item.description: Ireland struck three times in the first half to cruise to a 3-0 Nations League victory over Israel on Sunday after a fraught weekend for the team following goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu’s withdrawal from the squad amid a dispute over whether to play the match.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ireland struck three times in the first half to cruise to a 3-0 Nations League victory over Israel on Sunday after a fraught weekend for the team following goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu’s withdrawal from the squad amid a dispute over whether to play the match. Ireland has been one of Europe's most outspoken critics of Israel's war in Gaza , and protests calling for the team to boycott the fixture prompted Bazunu to make himself unavailable. The game went ahead only after a majority of the Irish players voted to play. Shlomi Barzel, the Israeli Football Association's communications chief, said on Saturday that “football has won” after the players decided to fulfil the fixture despite calls for a boycott. Bazunu's withdrawal led coach Heimir Hallgrimsson to name defender Jimmy Dunne as Ireland’s emergency third goalkeeper. The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has also faced [USN:L6N45I06Z TEXT:"fierce criticism"] from fans and political figures, many of whom accused it of failing to provide the players with sufficient direction. With Israel's home games taking place in Debrecen, Hungary's second-largest city, the game unfolded in a subdued atmosphere reminiscent of the latter stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, when attendance restrictions left stadiums largely empty. There were a few hundred Israeli supporters and a handful of Irish fans in the ground, and the shouts of coaches and players could be clearly heard throughout. The Irish players wore black armbands in memory of all those killed in the conflict and bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem. There was no exchange of pennants or pre-match handshakes. Striker Troy Parrott netted the opener in the 14th minute, with Adam Idah scoring two minutes later and Jack Moylan adding a well-taken third in the 25th minute. BLACK ARMBAND Moylan ran towards the corner flag after scoring and removed his black armband before kissing it and the badge on his shirt as supporters in the stand booed. After losing their opening game 1-0 to Kosovo on Thursday, Ireland enjoyed a much-needed boost. They are now third in the group on three points, three behind leaders Austria, who beat second-placed Kosovo 3-1 earlier in the day. Any relief provided by the victory, however, may prove short-lived. Angered by the decision to play, many Irish supporters chose not to watch the match. Public broadcaster RTE featured no studio panel and no analysis, nor did the station sell any advertising around its coverage. FAI chief executive David Courell said a significant majority of the squad had voted to fulfil the fixtures. "Based on that, the association took the decision on behalf of Irish football that this fixture would continue, as we have always intended to fulfil the fixtures," he told a media conference on Saturday. Ireland are due to face Israel again on October 4 in a nominal [USN:L8N42G1NS TEXT:"home fixture"] that has been moved to Serbia and will be played behind closed doors, meaning the debate over whether the national team should face Israel is almost certain to reignite.

item.title: Defender Le Normand replaces injured Garcia in Spain squad
item.description: Defender Robin Le Normand has been called up to Spain's squad to replace the injured Eric Garcia, the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) announced on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Defender Robin Le Normand has been called up to Spain's squad to replace the injured Eric Garcia, the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) announced on Sunday. Barcelona defender Garcia withdrew from the line-up for Spain's 3-2 victory over England at Wembley on Saturday after suffering an injury during the warm-up. "Atletico Madrid player Robin Le Normand replaces Eric Garcia in the Spanish national team camp," the RFEF said in a statement. "The FC Barcelona centre-back felt some discomfort in his left knee and, after the tests carried out, it has been decided to withdraw him from the squad due to the proximity of the upcoming international matches, thus avoiding any risk and preserving the player's health," it added. The 29-year-old Le Normand, who has won 27 caps for Spain, missed the country's World Cup-winning campaign in June and July. Garcia, 25, was part of the victorious squad and made his only appearance of the tournament in the final against Argentina. Spain host Croatia on Tuesday and the Czech Republic on October 3 before travelling to face Croatia three days later in Nations League Group A3.

item.title: Netanyahu visitó Abu Dabi el domingo, según un responsable israelí
item.description: El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, visitó Abu Dabi y se reunió el domingo con el presidente de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, el jeque Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, según informó a Reuters un alto cargo israelí.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, visitó Abu Dabi y se reunió el domingo con el presidente de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, el jeque Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, según informó a Reuters un alto cargo israelí. Ni la oficina de Netanyahu ni el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos hicieron declaraciones al respecto de inmediato. La visita se produce después de que el periódico israelí Haaretz informara este mes de que el jeque Mohamed había advertido a Netanyahu una semana y media antes del 7 de octubre de 2023 de que Hamás estaba planeando una operación de gran envergadura contra Israel. Según Haaretz, la advertencia no se transmitió a los servicios de inteligencia ni al ejército israelíes. Netanyahu, que ha desmentido la noticia y ha amenazado con emprender acciones legales contra el periódico, se enfrenta a una dura campaña de reelección. Los líderes de la oposición han acusado al primer ministro de ser responsable de los fallos de seguridad que precedieron al ataque de Hamás del 7 de octubre. Los Emiratos Árabes Unidos se han negado a comentar la noticia de Haaretz, pero han afirmado que los Emiratos e Israel han mantenido "líneas de comunicación abiertas y directas" desde que establecieron relaciones diplomáticas en 2020. Una fuente de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos declaró anteriormente a Reuters que el país aborda cuestiones de seguridad con otros países a través de las "entidades pertinentes", pero no "a nivel de los líderes nacionales". A principios de este año, los EAU negaron que el presidente, el jeque Mohamed, se hubiera reunido con Netanyahu después de que la oficina del primer ministro israelí afirmara en mayo que Netanyahu había "visitado en secreto" el país del Golfo y se había reunido con el presidente. Una fuente familiarizada con la reunión afirmó en aquel momento que Netanyahu y el jeque Mohamed se reunieron en Al-Ain, una ciudad-oasis de Abu Dabi situada en la frontera del país con Omán, el 26 de marzo. Desde que fue objeto de ataques durante la guerra con Irán, los EAU han reforzado sus relaciones con Estados Unidos e Israel, con los que establecieron vínculos a raíz de los Acuerdos de Abraham de 2020. La relación con Israel proporciona a los EAU una palanca de influencia regional y un canal único hacia Washington.

item.title: Francisco Lindor hits 300th HR, but Mets drop finale to Nats
item.description: Andres Chaparro had three hits, including two solo home runs, and the Nationals beat the New York Mets 6-4 on Sunday in Washington to end their season with a series win.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Andres Chaparro had three hits, including two solo home runs, and the Nationals beat the New York Mets 6-4 on Sunday in Washington to end their season with a series win. Will Dion (3-2) pitched two scoreless innings for the victory and Erik Tolman worked the ninth for his fifth save for Washington (77-85), which improved by 11 wins over 2025. Francisco Lindor hit his 300th career homer and Ronny Mauricio smacked his third home run in two games for the Mets (74-88), who finished last in the National League East. Carson Benge ended his rookie season with three hits and an RBI. Juan Soto, who left in the ninth inning Saturday after being hit on the right hand by a pitch, went 0-for-5. Mets starter Sean Manaea (6-8) gave up five runs on seven hits over six innings. Lindor led off the game with a single, went to second on a wild pitch and scored on a Benge single. In the bottom half, Brady House walked and scored on a triple by CJ Abrams, his 106th RBI. Luis Torrens walked with one out in the New York second, and Mauricio homered in his third straight at-bat to make it 3-1. Lindor followed with his 300th home run to become the first primary shortstop in major league history with 300 homers and 200 stolen bases. Washington pulled within 4-2 in the bottom of the second when Harry Ford doubled with two outs and scored on a double by Nasim Nunez. Chaparro homered leading off the bottom of the third to make it 4-3. Dylan Crews doubled with two outs and scored the tying run on a Jacob Young single. Chaparro led off the fifth with his second homer and 13th of the season and the Nationals led 5-4. With runners on first and second and two outs in the sixth, Riley Cornelio picked Mauricio off at second. In the seventh, James Wood walked, went to third on a Chaparro single and scored on House's single to make it 6-4. Washington's DJ Herz, in his second start since returning from Tommy John surgery, gave up four runs on six hits over three innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Greece stun Germany 1-0 in losing home debut for Klopp
item.description: Greece scored a 74th-minute goal through Dimitris Kourbelis to stun hosts Germany 1-0 in their Nations League Group A2 on Sunday to top the group and spoil coach Juergen Klopp's home debut on the German bench.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Greece scored a 74th-minute goal through Dimitris Kourbelis to stun hosts Germany 1-0 in their Nations League Group A2 on Sunday to top the group and spoil coach Juergen Klopp's home debut on the German bench. It was the first ever victory for the Greeks in 11 matches against the Germans, and they now lead their group on six points from two matches. Germany are on one point. The hosts were in control for most of the game and had close to 80% possession in the first half alone but they were ultimately punished for sloppy defending, especially in the second half, which gave the Greeks space to attack. Klopp, who [USN:L1N43Q095 TEXT:"took over"] in July after Germany's early World Cup exit, has now failed to win either of his two matches in charge following a 1-1 draw against the Dutch in Amsterdam on Thursday. "I could have lived with us not winning but you cannot lose such a game," Klopp said. "We have been together for a week now, all mixed together, and that needs time. "The result is not cool but it is absolutely part of the process," he said. Germany next play Serbia on Thursday before travelling to Greece three days later. TWO WINS IN A ROW FOR GREECE Despite enjoying a dominant first half it was only after they upped their tempo and started pressing higher that Germany carved out scoring chances. Felix Nmecha fired wide in the 54th, a minute after Greece keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis had palmed a Joshua Kimmich free kick over the bar. The Greeks, however, almost scored in the 66th after Kimmich lost possession in his own half but substitute Fotis Ioannidis fired just wide of the post. They did better in the 74th with Kourbelis' deflected low drive that gave them the win to make it two victories in a row after their last-gasp 2-1 win over Serbia on Thursday. In the same group, Netherlands earned a 2-1 victory over Serbia thanks to Mexx Meerdink's double strike on his second appearance for his country. It was the first win under new coach Xavi Hernandez following [USN:L6N45G1AO TEXT:"their draw"] with Germany on Thursday. “It's a boyhood dream. I actually don't have any words for it," Meerdink said. "Everything is happening so quickly. You just don't realise what can happen in the space of a week. It's also great that we managed to win here. “Sometimes you need a bit of luck. This time it went my way. Then you have to be there and be important for the team. I did feel a little pressure, I was a bit nervous. But you play that out of your system. And then to be allowed to score two is fantastic." Joao Felix scored for the second consecutive Nations League match as defending champions Portugal, with Cristiano Ronaldo on the bench throughout, edged past hosts Norway 2-1 to top Group A4 with two wins from two matches so far. The Norwegians cancelled out Felix's 17th-minute lead with Erling Haaland's equaliser before Goncalo Ramos' chip won it for the visitors. Ben Davies scored a 53rd-minute own goal and Gustav Isaksen added another on the hour as Denmark eased past Wales 2-0 to earn their first points in Group A4. In a [USN:L1N45I02P TEXT:"politically charged "]encounter in Group B3, Ireland scored twice in three minutes early in the first half to [USN:L6N45J074 TEXT:"ease past"] Israel 3-0.

item.title: Marcus Mariota helps Commanders chop down Seahawks
item.description: Marcus Mariota threw three touchdown passes, Kain Medrano returned an interception 50 yards for a score late in the fourth quarter and the Washington Commanders held on to shock the defending champion Seattle Seahawks 33-31 Sunday in Landover, Md.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Marcus Mariota threw three touchdown passes, Kain Medrano returned an interception 50 yards for a score late in the fourth quarter and the Washington Commanders held on to shock the defending champion Seattle Seahawks 33-31 Sunday in Landover, Md. Mariota, starting in place of the injured Jayden Daniels (elbow), was 19-of-31 passing for 183 yards and no interceptions. Terry McLaurin had six catches for 77 yards and a score for the Commanders (1-2) in their home opener. Sam Darnold, injured in the first quarter of Seattle's opener, was 31 of 45 for 379 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions in his return. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 10 catches for 128 yards and two scores. Medrano picked off Darnold's check-down pass over the middle and scored to make it 33-24 with 3:57 remaining. The extra point attempt failed after a sideline celebration penalty. Darnold completed five straight passes, the last a 7-yard TD to Cooper Kupp with 2:51 remaining, and it was 33-31. But Rachaad White ran for 19 yards on third down and Mariota ran for another first down to ice it. Seattle (2-1) had won 12 straight games, including playoffs, beginning with Week 12 of last season. The Seahawks, who allowed 17 points over their first two games, did not have a takeaway and turned the ball over three times. With the Commanders leading 17-10 early in the third quarter, Darnold's pass deflected off a defensive lineman and was picked off by Sonny Styles. Three plays later, Mariota hit McLaurin for a 30-yard touchdown and Washington led 24-10. Seattle started at its own 40 after the kickoff went out of bounds. Eight plays later, Darnold pulled Seattle within 24-17 when he connected with Eric Saubert for a 13-yard touchdown. Early in the fourth quarter, a Seahawks drive that included a 16-yard pass from Smith-Njigba to George Holani was capped by an 11-yard Darnold touchdown pass to Smith-Njigba, his sixth TD of the year. The Commanders started at their own 40. On fourth-and-1, Mariota hit McLaurin for six yards and then found Stefon Diggs for 10. Drew Stevens converted a field goal from 36 yards to give Washington a 27-24 lead with 4:34 remaining. Washington recovered a fumble on the Seattle 21 early in the game. The Commanders capitalized four plays later when Mariota passed 6 yards to White for a touchdown. Late in the quarter, Seattle marched 90 yards in nine plays. Tight end AJ Barner rumbled 32 yards with a screen pass and Darnold found Smith-Njigba for the tying touchdown with 13:27 left in the half. The Commanders answered as Jaylin Lane's 21-yard catch and run got them to the 12 and Mariota passed 11 yards to Treylon Burks to give Washington a 14-7 lead at the 6:47 mark. Darnold drove the Seahawks to a first-and-goal at the 5, but his fourth-down pass was incomplete. Seattle's Jason Myers and Stevens traded 57-yard field goals in the final minute. Washington linebacker Leo Chenal was taken off on the cart in the second quarter with a neck injury. --Field Level Media

item.title: Deshaun Watson guides Browns to comeback win over Panthers
item.description: Deshaun Watson returned after a brief time on the sideline to help rescue the Cleveland Browns with a 14-yard touchdown pass to Harold Fannin Jr. with 1:48 remaining in a home-opening, 21-18 victory against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Deshaun Watson returned after a brief time on the sideline to help rescue the Cleveland Browns with a 14-yard touchdown pass to Harold Fannin Jr. with 1:48 remaining in a home-opening, 21-18 victory against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday afternoon. After the go-ahead TD toss, Watson threw to Denzel Boston for the two-point conversion. The Panthers failed to pick up a first down on the ensuing possession, but got the ball back with 1:01 left when the Browns were stopped on fourth-and-1 at the Carolina 15. Nearing midfield, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young was intercepted by Ronnie Hickman to seal the outcome. Fannin caught seven passes for 51 yards and both of Watson's touchdown throws. Watson was 16-for-30 passing for 144 yards for the Browns (2-1). Young went 26-for-48 for 290 yards with one touchdown. Ryan Fitzgerald kicked four field goals for the Panthers (1-2). The Panthers' only touchdown came on Young's 8-yard pass to John Metchie III with 4:25 remaining to complete a six-play, 72-yard drive. Carolina led 18-13 after a two-point attempt failed. The Browns reached the Carolina 24 before a penalty pushed them back. But Akayleb Evans' interception of Watson in the end zone was nullified by a roughing-the-passer penalty, and Watson exited with an unspecified injury. So the Browns, with a first-and-10 at the Panthers' 14, summoned Shedeur Sanders, making his season debut, for one play prior to the two-minute warning before Watson returned. Sanders threw a completion for no gain, two plays before Watson connected with Fannin. The Browns had 154 yards of total offense through three quarters, yet led 10-9. Carolina took its first lead on Fitzgerald's 37-yard boot with 11:41 to play for a 12-10 edge. The Browns moved 44 yards to set up Andre Szmyt's 45-yard field goal to retake the lead with 7:30 left. The Panthers scored more than 30 points in each of their first two games, but the points were tougher to come by against the Browns. Cleveland opened the scoring on Szmyt's 48-yard field goal with 5:43 remaining in the second quarter. Watson's 2-yard pass to Fannin for a touchdown came with 1:37 to play in the first half. But Carolina made efficient use of nine plays to move in range for Fitzgerald's 35-yard field goal before halftime. Fitzgerald added a 41-yarder to end the first possession of the second half. He was good from 53 yards later in the third quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Yankees, Orioles won’t play Game 162 as storm scraps finale
item.description: The New York Yankees and visiting Baltimore Orioles, in conjunction with Major League Baseball, decided to call off their regular-season finale Sunday due to continued inclement weather from this weekend's nor'easter.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The New York Yankees and visiting Baltimore Orioles, in conjunction with Major League Baseball, decided to call off their regular-season finale Sunday due to continued inclement weather from this weekend's nor'easter. The game would not have had an impact on the MLB playoffs. The Yankees were already locked into the No. 4 seed -- the first wild card -- with the Tampa Bay Rays clinching the AL East title earlier this week. The Yankees completed the regular season with a 93-68 record. They will host the rival Boston Red Sox in a best-of-three AL wild-card series starting Tuesday. The Orioles finished 79-82 and fourth in the AL East under new manager Craig Albernaz. Baltimore experienced its second straight losing season after winning 275 games from 2022-24. New York and Baltimore moved Saturday's scheduled game to Friday and played a doubleheader, which the teams split. Alonso homered twice in Baltimore's 10-2 win during the first game before the Yankees scored four runs in the sixth inning of a 6-3 victory in the nightcap for the split. Sunday's game was originally moved up two hours to a 1:05 p.m. start time, but rain continued to hit New York throughout the afternoon. --Field Level Media

item.content:encoded: Israël a annoncé dimanche qu'il révoquait le statut diplomatique des diplomates néerlandais représentant les Pays-Bas auprès de l'Autorité palestinienne, dont le siège se trouve à Ramallah, en réponse aux sanctions néerlandaises visant les colonies israéliennes en Cisjordanie occupée. Au début du mois, Israël Israël a ordonné la fermeture du [USN:L8N45010Q TEXT:"consulat britannique"] de Jérusalem-Est, accrédité auprès de l'Autorité palestinienne, en réponse aux [USN:L6N4500FE TEXT:"restrictions commerciales"] imposées par douze pays, dont le Royaume-Uni, sur les biens issus des colonies en Cisjordanie occupée. Le ministre israélien des Affaires étrangères, Gideon Saar, a déclaré que les diplomates néerlandais en poste à Ramallah devaient restituer leurs documents diplomatiques délivrés par Israël dans un délai de sept jours, date à laquelle leurs privilèges et immunités diplomatiques expireront. "Tout pays qui agit de manière hostile et unilatérale à l'encontre d'Israël perdra son influence et sa pertinence dans la région", a-t-il dit sur la plate-forme X. Le ministère néerlandais des Affaires étrangères n'a pas souhaité faire de commentaire.

item.title: Steelers win shootout to hand Bengals first loss
item.description: Chris Boswell booted the go-ahead field goal and Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow in the final minute to lift the host Pittsburgh Steelers to a 30-27 win over the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Chris Boswell booted the go-ahead field goal and Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow in the final minute to lift the host Pittsburgh Steelers to a 30-27 win over the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. Pittsburgh (2-1) took a 30-27 lead with 2:15 left when Boswell connected from 33 yards, six and a half minutes after he tied the game with a 36-yard kick. Aaron Rodgers was 19-of-34 passing for 292 yards and three touchdowns to lead the Steelers. Burrow, who completed his first 14 passes for 96 yards, finished 28-of-37 for 282 yards and three touchdowns for Cincinnati (2-1). Ja'Marr Chase grabbed nine receptions for 98 yards and a first-quarter score, while Tee Higgins added six for 90 yards and a touchdown. Facing fourth-and-2 at the Steelers' 25, Burrow found tight end Mike Gesicki in stride as he blew past three defensive backs in the Pittsburgh secondary and made the full-extension grab while keeping his feet in. The catch with 13:29 to play put the Bengals on top 27-24 in the seesaw second half. Rodgers directed the Steelers to first half leads of 7-0, 14-7 and 17-10. His first pass of the game went for 30 yards on a short cross over the middle to Jaylen Warren. He finished his first drive with a perfect lob to Roman Wilson for 38 yards and a touchdown. Rodgers also found Ben Skowronek for a wide-open touchdown of 23 yards after Skowronek made a double move on safety Jordan Battle. With Pittsburgh up 17-10 and driving for another score thanks to a defensive hold called on Cincinnati corner Tacario Davis, Rodgers had a pass over the middle deflect off the hands of Wilson and into the hands of Battle. The Bengals needed five plays to drive 53 yards for the tying score, with Higgins making a circus touchdown catch while sitting in the end zone to secure a 17-17 halftime tie. After a 38-yard Evan McPherson field goal gave the Bengals their first lead, the Steelers got a massive break when Cedric Johnson was called for a personal foul roughing the kicker when he slid into punter Cameron Johnston's plant leg. Seven plays later, Rodgers found a wide-open DK Metcalf in the back of the end zone after defensive backs DJ Turner and Dax Hill ran into each other. The Bengals lost a pair of key players in the first half, one on each side of the ball. Rookie receiver Colbie Young injured his right knee on the first offensive play of the game when Jaquan Brisker brought him to the ground. Bengals safety Bryan Cook injured his right ankle on Cincinnati's second defensive series and came out before halftime, replaced by Kyle Dugger. --Field Level Media

item.title: Colts kick losing streak, take down Texans
item.description: Spencer Shrader kicked four field goals, including a 53-yarder with 16 seconds remaining, to lead the Indianapolis Colts to a 19-17 victory over the visiting Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Spencer Shrader kicked four field goals, including a 53-yarder with 16 seconds remaining, to lead the Indianapolis Colts to a 19-17 victory over the visiting Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon. Shrader matched his career best of 58 yards to help the Colts (1-2) snap a five-game losing streak against their AFC South rivals. Daniel Jones was 24-of-36 passing for 235 yards, one touchdown, one interception and two lost fumbles for the Colts. Keenan Allen caught a touchdown pass and Indianapolis halted a nine-game overall skid dating back to last season. Will Anderson Jr. recorded 2.5 sacks, forced one fumble and recovered another for the Texans (0-3), who didn't commit a turnover while forcing three Indianapolis miscues. C.J. Stroud completed 16 of 27 passes for 167 yards and one touchdown for Houston. Foster Moreau had a scoring reception and Woody Marks added a rushing score. The Texans also started 0-3 last season before recovering to make the playoffs. Houston was outgained 300 to 223. Marks scored on a 1-yard run with 1:48 remaining to give Houston a 17-16 lead. The touchdown was set up by Anderson, who sacked Jones and forced a fumble that Tommy Togiai recovered at the Texans' 46-yard line with 4:40 left. The Texans traveled 54 yards on seven plays with Marks scoring from the 1, and Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked the extra point that gave Houston its first lead. The Texans were unable to get into position for a late field goal. Houston was without stellar wideout Nico Collins (hamstring) for the second consecutive game. Shrader kicked a 37-yard field goal with 12:43 remaining to give Indianapolis a 16-7 advantage. Houston again made it a one-score game when Fairbairn booted a 24-yard field goal with 7:33 to play. The Colts held Houston to 67 first-half yards and led 13-7 at the break. Indianapolis got on the board first. Shrader kicked a 39-yard field goal with 4:28 left in the opening quarter. Jones tossed a 6-yard touchdown pass to Allen to make it 10-0 with 11:08 remaining in the second quarter. The Texans narrowed their deficit to three when Stroud tossed a 1-yard scoring pass to Moreau with 4:30 left. Shrader then connected on the 58-yard field goal with 1:03 remaining in the half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Josh Allen, Bills rally back to keep Chargers winless
item.description: Josh Allen ran for a pair of 1-yard touchdown runs, including the go-ahead score in the fourth quarter, as the Buffalo Bills rallied for a 24-16 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday at Orchard Park, N.Y.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Josh Allen ran for a pair of 1-yard touchdown runs, including the go-ahead score in the fourth quarter, as the Buffalo Bills rallied for a 24-16 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday at Orchard Park, N.Y. Allen was 16-of-26 passing for 204 yards while overcoming two first-half interceptions. He added eight carries for 22 yards and has scored two rushing touchdowns in each of his three games this season. James Cook III added 154 rushing yards on 24 carries with a touchdown as Buffalo (3-0), despite five turnovers, won its second game in two weeks at its new $2 billion stadium. Justin Herbert was 20-of-34 passing for 226 yards with a touchdown and an interception for the Chargers (0-3). Omarion Hampton rushed for 56 yards on 15 carries, and Genesis Smith had two interceptions for Los Angeles. Herbert's interception came at the Bills' goal line early in the fourth quarter from C.J. Gardner-Johnson, who returned it 41 yards. Buffalo then went on a 13-play, 58-yard drive that included a lost fumble from Allen which was wiped away on a Chargers penalty. Allen scored his go-ahead TD for a 17-13 lead with 7:35 remaining. The Chargers turned their opening drive of the game into a 7-0 lead by going 47 yards in eight plays and getting a 1-yard touchdown pass from Herbert to Keaton Mitchell. Los Angeles increased the lead to 10-0 on a 31-yard field goal from Cameron Dicker late in the first quarter. The Bills took charge of the second quarter, getting a 28-yard field goal from Tyler Bass before going into the half with a 10-10 tie after a 1-yard TD run from Allen. A beleaguered Chargers defense was much improved in the first half by forcing two Allen interceptions and recovering a fumble. The Chargers regained the lead 13-10 on a 21-yard field goal from Dicker midway through the third quarter. Los Angeles ran seven plays in the red zone but could not find the end zone. After Allen's second 1-yard score in the fourth put Buffalo on top, the Bills made it 24-13 with 3:13 remaining on a 3-yard run from Cook. The drive started after Los Angeles turned the ball over on downs after a dropped pass by Kimani Vidal with 5:14 to go. Dicker made a 33-yard field goal with 1:59 remaining, but the Chargers failed to recover the ensuing onside kick. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kenneth Walker III scores twice as Chiefs control Dolphins
item.description: Kenneth Walker III had a rushing and receiving touchdown and Patrick Mahomes threw for 246 yards and two scores with one interception as the Kansas City Chiefs topped the Miami Dolphins 24-10 on Sunday in Miami Gardens, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kenneth Walker III had a rushing and receiving touchdown and Patrick Mahomes threw for 246 yards and two scores with one interception as the Kansas City Chiefs topped the Miami Dolphins 24-10 on Sunday in Miami Gardens, Fla. The Dolphins (0-3) trailed by one score until the closing minutes. Miami lost by 14 and 22 points, respectively, in the first two weeks. Miami failed to convert a fourth-and-5 from its own 48 with 5:56 remaining, with Malik Willis throwing incomplete for Kevin Coleman. The Chiefs (3-0) took over and sealed the game on an 11-yard touchdown pass from Mahomes to Travis Kelce with 2:55 to go. George Karlaftis intercepted Willis on the Dolphins' ensuing possession. The Dolphins held the ball for 34:21 compared to 25:39 for the Chiefs but turned the ball over on downs three times. Mahomes was 20-of-24 passing with an interception. Willis finished 20 for 36 for 210 yards while leading the Dolphins with 56 yards rushing on nine carries. Chris Bell had four catches for 67 yards. Walker gained 70 yards on 18 carries. Rashee Rice topped the Chiefs with seven catches for 88 yards. Kansas City and Miami combined to score touchdowns on the first three drives of the game. Walker opened the scoring with a 10-yard touchdown run just 2:06 into the game. Miami responded with a 17-play, 91-yard drive that took 9:27 off the clock. Ollie Gordon II scored on a run from 3 yards out. The Dolphins played most of the game without running back De'Von Achane, who sustained a knee injury during the team's first series. Achane was slow to get to his feet following a tackle from Alohi Gilman and needed trainers' assistance to leave the field. Initially ruled questionable to return, Achane was downgraded to out late in the second quarter. He gained 17 yards on three carries. The Chiefs went ahead 14-7 with 12:58 left in the second quarter, as Mahomes connected with Walker for a 5-yard touchdown. Mahomes completed his first 12 passes. His lone incompletion came with 1:50 remaining in the second quarter. With the Chiefs aiming to take advantage of a Willis fumble, Mahomes threw behind Rice. The ball was deflected and intercepted on a diving play by Jacob Rodriguez. Kansas City went ahead 17-10 on Harrison Butker's 34-yard field goal with 11:35 left, capping a drive that started at the Chiefs' 4-yard line. Butker missed a 50-yard field goal attempt wide left with 57 seconds left. --Field Level Media

item.title: Defense, Cam Skattebo lead way as Giants hold off Titans
item.description: Dominic Zvada kicked four field goals and the New York Giants' defense held the Tennessee Titans to one first down in the first half of a 12-7 win on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Dominic Zvada kicked four field goals and the New York Giants' defense held the Tennessee Titans to one first down in the first half of a 12-7 win on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J. Zvada hit from 39, 27, 39 and 30 yards on a rainy, windy afternoon at MetLife Stadium. New York's defense did the rest, forcing Tennessee to punt five consecutive times in the first half and keeping it out of the end zone until 5:35 remained in the fourth quarter. Cam Ward found Wan'Dale Robinson for a 4-yard touchdown strike that gave the Titans (0-3) a chance. They forced a punt and got the ball back at their 23 with 3:03 remaining, eventually reaching the Giants' 7 on Ward's 11-yard completion to Elic Ayomanor with 24 seconds left. But Jevon Holland preserved the win for the Giants (2-1) by intercepting Ward with 17 seconds on the clock. Ward connected on 23 of 36 passes for 181 yards, while Tony Pollard rushed for a game-high 74 yards on 17 carries. Jameis Winston completed 14 of 22 passes for 118 yards for New York in his first start after Jaxson Dart went down Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams with a season-ending knee injury. New York opened the scoring with 6:34 left in the first quarter on Zvada's first 39-yard field goal, which capped a 50-yard drive. Winston found Cam Skattebo for a 30-yard completion to key the drive. Zvada increased the advantage to 6-0 with 4:49 left in the half, converting from 27 yards out to finish off a 44-yard drive that chewed up seven minutes, 10 seconds of clock. Tennessee finally moved the chains with 1:18 left in the half on a 16-yard pass from Ward to Robinson. But the drive stalled and the Titans settled for a 59-yard field goal attempt by Joey Slye that missed. Given that field position, the Giants maneuvered down to the Titans' 21 and Zvada hit from 39 for a 9-0 halftime lead. Zvada added his 30-yarder with 6:56 to go in the third quarter. Skattebo finished with 100 yards from scrimmage: 60 rushing yards on 20 carries and 40 receiving yards on three catches. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs scores 3 TDs as Lions survive Jets with late takeaway
item.description: Jahmyr Gibbs scored three touchdowns and totaled 164 yards and the Lions made a stop to end a shootout in the final minute and defeat the New York Jets 31-24 on Sunday in Detroit.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jahmyr Gibbs scored three touchdowns and totaled 164 yards and the Lions made a stop to end a shootout in the final minute and defeat the New York Jets 31-24 on Sunday in Detroit. The Lions reclaimed the lead with 2:25 remaining. Gibbs caught a Jared Goff swing pass at the line of scrimmage in the right flat and jogged in from 11 yards out in an apparent blown coverage by the Jets. New York drove inside the 30 of the Lions before Garrett Wilson, who had 10 receptions for 107 yards and a fourth-quarter TD, required medical attention. Wilson was hit by Ennis Rakestraw and Chuck Clark as a Geno Smith pass arrived. The injury with 51 seconds left cost the Jets their final timeout. On the next play, Smith was sacked by Clark near the 33 on a jailbreak blitz up the middle and fumbled. Jack Campbell scooped up the ball to end the game. It was New York's first turnover of the game. Smith had thrown for touchdowns on the previous two fourth-quarter drives and finished with three TD passes and 321 yards on 31-of-37 passing. Jets rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq caught seven passes for 105 yards and TD. Goff was 25 of 32 for 269 yards and two TDs. Gibbs had 20 carries for 99 yards and two rushing touchdowns and caught seven passes for 65 yards with a score. A gamble on fourth down with around eight minutes left and an eight-point lead backfired on the Lions. Gibbs was hit behind the line of scrimmage, turning the ball over on downs to the Jets at their own 45. Smith converted on fourth-and-6 at the Detroit 23 with 4:11 left. He hit Wilson down the right sideline for a touchdown, then tied the game at 24 with the two-point pass to Sterling Shepard.
